from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Metadata
        title_text = "The Mathematical Fragmentations"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Traditional math notation for exponents is fragmented.",
            "We use separate symbols for powers, roots, and logarithms.",
            "Observe how 2, 3, and 8 shift around confusingly.",
            "Superscripts, radicals, and 'log' labels feel disconnected.",
            "What if we could unify these three distinct forms?"
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors from Animation Description
        color_x = "#3498DB" # Blue (Base / Root / Log base)
        color_y = "#E74C3C" # Red (Exponent / Degree / Log result)
        color_z = "#2ECC71" # Green (Result / Radicand / Log argument)
        highlight_color = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Traditional math notation for exponents is fragmented.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(highlight_color))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # We use separate symbols for powers, roots, and logarithms.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(highlight_color)
        )
        
        # Create formulas with variables x, y, z
        formula_power = MathTex("x", "^", "{y}", "=", "z")
        formula_root = MathTex("\\sqrt[", "y", "]{", "z", "}", "=", "x")
        formula_log = MathTex("\\log", "_", "x", "(", "z", ")", "=", "y")
        
        # Color variables
        for f in [formula_power, formula_root, formula_log]:
            f.set_color_by_tex("x", color_x)
            f.set_color_by_tex("y", color_y)
            f.set_color_by_tex("z", color_z)

        self.place_in_area(formula_power, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_in_area(formula_root, "C2", "C5", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_in_area(formula_log, "D2", "D5", scale_factor=1.2)

        self.play(FadeIn(formula_power), FadeIn(formula_root), FadeIn(formula_log))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Observe how 2, 3, and 8 shift around confusingly.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(highlight_color)
        )
        
        # Numbers 2, 3, 8
        num_power = MathTex("2", "^", "3", "=", "8")
        num_root = MathTex("\\sqrt[", "3", "]{", "8", "}", "=", "2")
        num_log = MathTex("\\log", "_", "2", "(", "8", ")", "=", "3")
        
        for n in [num_power, num_root, num_log]:
            n.set_color_by_tex("2", color_x)
            n.set_color_by_tex("3", color_y)
            n.set_color_by_tex("8", color_z)

        self.place_in_area(num_power, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_in_area(num_root, "C2", "C5", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_in_area(num_log, "D2", "D5", scale_factor=1.2)

        self.play(
            Transform(formula_power, num_power),
            Transform(formula_root, num_root),
            Transform(formula_log, num_log)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Draw arrows showing how 2, 3, 8 move between positions.
        # Use specific parts of the MathTex for accuracy. 
        # In num_power: 2 is part [0], 3 is part [2], 8 is part [4]
        # In num_root: 3 is part [1], 8 is part [3], 2 is part [6]
        # In num_log: 2 is part [2], 8 is part [4], 3 is part [7]

        # Arrows from Power to Root
        arrow_2_root = CurvedArrow(formula_power[0].get_center(), formula_root[6].get_center(), angle=-PI/4, color=color_x)
        arrow_3_root = CurvedArrow(formula_power[2].get_center(), formula_root[1].get_center(), angle=PI/4, color=color_y)
        arrow_8_root = CurvedArrow(formula_power[4].get_center(), formula_root[3].get_center(), angle=-PI/4, color=color_z)

        self.play(Create(arrow_2_root), Create(arrow_3_root), Create(arrow_8_root))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(arrow_2_root), FadeOut(arrow_3_root), FadeOut(arrow_8_root))

        # Arrows from Power to Log
        arrow_2_log = CurvedArrow(formula_power[0].get_center(), formula_log[2].get_center(), angle=-PI/3, color=color_x)
        arrow_3_log = CurvedArrow(formula_power[2].get_center(), formula_log[7].get_center(), angle=PI/3, color=color_y)
        arrow_8_log = CurvedArrow(formula_power[4].get_center(), formula_log[4].get_center(), angle=-PI/3, color=color_z)

        self.play(Create(arrow_2_log), Create(arrow_3_log), Create(arrow_8_log))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(arrow_2_log), FadeOut(arrow_3_log), FadeOut(arrow_8_log))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Superscripts, radicals, and 'log' labels feel disconnected.
        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(highlight_color)
        )
        
        # Highlight fragmented symbols: superscript caret/pos, radical, 'log'
        rect_pow = SurroundingRectangle(formula_power[1], color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        rect_root = SurroundingRectangle(formula_root[0], color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        rect_log = SurroundingRectangle(formula_log[0], color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Create(rect_pow), Create(rect_root), Create(rect_log))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(rect_pow), FadeOut(rect_root), FadeOut(rect_log))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # What if we could unify these three distinct forms?
        self.play(
            self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(highlight_color)
        )
        
        # Fade out formulas leaving only the colored variables x, y, z
        var_x = MathTex("x", color=color_x)
        var_y = MathTex("y", color=color_y)
        var_z = MathTex("z", color=color_z)
        
        self.place_at_grid(var_x, "C2", scale_factor=2.0)
        self.place_at_grid(var_y, "C4", scale_factor=2.0)
        self.place_at_grid(var_z, "C6", scale_factor=2.0)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(formula_power),
            FadeOut(formula_root),
            FadeOut(formula_log),
            FadeIn(var_x),
            FadeIn(var_y),
            FadeIn(var_z)
        )
        self.wait(3)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class Section1Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout (Title and Lecture Notes)
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        title_text = "The Triangle of Power: Unified Notation"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Connects Powers, Roots, and Logs",
            "- Visual representation of $x^y = z$",
            "- High mathematical symmetry",
            "- Simplified algebraic manipulation"
        ]

        title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(title)

        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        lecture_group = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        lecture_group.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(lecture_group, shift=RIGHT))

        # 2. Define 6x6 Animation Grid (Right Side)
        grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]
        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Offset grid to the right half of the screen
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.9 
                y = 1.8 - i * 0.9
                grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        # 3. Create the Triangle of Power
        # Vertices: Top (Exponent), Bottom-Left (Base), Bottom-Right (Result)
        top_v = grid["B3"]
        left_v = grid["E1"]
        right_v = grid["E5"]

        triangle = Polygon(top_v, left_v, right_v, color=BLUE, stroke_width=4)
        
        # Labels using MathTex and tex_to_color_map for consistency (Belief B050)
        label_base = MathTex("b", tex_to_color_map={"b": YELLOW}).move_to(left_v + LEFT * 0.4)
        label_exp = MathTex("e", tex_to_color_map={"e": RED}).move_to(top_v + UP * 0.4)
        label_val = MathTex("v", tex_to_color_map={"v": GREEN}).move_to(right_v + RIGHT * 0.4)

        # 4. Animation Sequence
        self.play(Create(triangle), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(
            Write(label_base),
            Write(label_exp),
            Write(label_val)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # 5. Show Relationships
        # Power: b^e = v
        eq_power = MathTex("b^e = v", tex_to_color_map={"b": YELLOW, "e": RED, "v": GREEN})
        eq_power.move_to(grid["F3"])
        
        # Create arrows pointing to relationships
        side_left = Line(top_v, left_v, color=RED_A)
        side_right = Line(top_v, right_v, color=GREEN_A)
        side_bottom = Line(left_v, right_v, color=YELLOW_A)

        self.play(side_bottom.animate.set_stroke(width=8), Write(eq_power))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(side_bottom.animate.set_stroke(width=4))

        # Root: e_root_v = b
        eq_root = MathTex("\\sqrt[e]{v} = b", tex_to_color_map={"b": YELLOW, "e": RED, "v": GREEN})
        eq_root.move_to(grid["F3"])
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(eq_power, eq_root),
            side_left.animate.set_stroke(width=8)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(side_left.animate.set_stroke(width=4))

        # Log: log_b(v) = e
        eq_log = MathTex("\\log_b(v) = e", tex_to_color_map={"b": YELLOW, "e": RED, "v": GREEN})
        eq_log.move_to(grid["F3"])

        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(eq_root, eq_log),
            side_right.animate.set_stroke(width=8)
        )
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(side_right.animate.set_stroke(width=4))

        # Final cleanup
        self.play(FadeOut(eq_log), triangle.animate.set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.2))
        self.wait(2)
